paragraphs.source_en: Hattori Hanzo had plainly grown much thinner. His two large eyes bulged with such frightening intensity that one scarcely dared meet them. His face was covered in a thick beard, and dark blotches marred even the whites of his eyes—he truly looked the part of his sobriquet, “Demon Hanzo.”

paragraphs.source_en: Imagawa Yoshimoto, who had given Lady Tsukiyama—Princess Sena—to Ieyasu in marriage, had departed this world. Ieyasu's father-in-law, Sekiguchi Gyobu Chikanaga, who had once eagerly welcomed him as a worthy son-in-law, had also been forced by Yoshimoto's son Ujizane to take his own life by seppuku. Where was Ujizane now, and what was he doing? Rumor had it that in Kyoto he was playing kemari for Nobunaga, the enemy who had killed his father...
